title: List submap bindings under the chord that enters their mode in the keybindings menu

leads.summary: Cache key v14 collides with the newer quattro tip; existing users do not receive prefixed mode rows
leads.consequence: Quattro f8146395 already changed the Lua scan and set the cache salt to v14. On a system that previously opened the menu, installing this PR with unchanged binds/keymap reuses the old non-prefixed records file. Menu and --print still show a mode's H as a global H, until binds/keymap change or cache is manually removed; only then the new sorting/prefix appears. Use a fresh cache version relative to the actual target branch (consider open PR #8229's v15 if it lands first).

leads.summary: A submap entered through a valid code: binding is not mapped, despite its entry row existing
leads.consequence: Hyprland's plain `bind = SUPER, code:49, submap, window` yields an empty `key:` and nonzero `keycode:`. add_submap_entry rejects the empty key, while dynamic_bindings later resolves the entry to SUPER + ~. Mode children therefore display `window > H` apart from that entry row instead of `SUPER + ~ > H`; the same raw-vs-resolved key difference affects some mouse entries. Read/recover keycode for entry binds and apply the same display normalization to the map and entry row.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q1 confirmed (q1-conf-keycode-entry.md); folded into F1 suggested change

leads.summary: Hyprland accepts opts.desc but the Lua source scan misses entry chords declared with that alias
leads.consequence: A user's `hl.bind('SUPER + P', hl.dsp.submap('window'), { desc = 'Window mode' })` appears as a named entry row in hyprctl binds, but the mock hl.bind checks only opts.description and writes no cache row. Since dispatcher is __lua, the plain-dispatcher fallback also misses it, and children fall back to `window > H` even though the entry row `SUPER + P` is visible. Accept desc as Hyprland does, with matching validation, or resolve entry from actual compositor data when possible.
leads.triage: Opus follow-up Q4 confirmed, pre-existing, low; not published

leads.summary: Removed or rebound Lua mode-entry binds remain in the source cache and mislabel the live mode rows
leads.consequence: If a user binds SUPER + P to enter window mode then removes it with hl.unbind (or o.rebind) and reuses SUPER + P for an unrelated action, Hyprland correctly reports only the replacement action, but the scanner's noop unbind retains the old source-derived hl.dsp.submap(window) entry. The new map therefore labels window > H as SUPER + P > H and sorts it under Replaced shortcut, although pressing SUPER + P no longer enters that mode. Use only registered live entry binds to validate the source-derived map, and model unbind/rebind or discard stale cache entries.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up Q2 confirmed (q2-stale-lua-entry.md); published in F1 with reproducer

leads.summary: Submap-universal bindings are wrongly described as requiring entry to the submap
leads.consequence: `bindu` in legacy configs and `{ submap_universal = true }` in Lua configs allow a bind registered under a named submap to fire even outside it. The new unconditional prefix says an extra entry chord is required for these binds, whereas users can press the chord directly. The plain `hyprctl binds` printer does not expose submap_universal even though the JSON printer includes it (and is malformed at v0.56.0), so distinguishing these rows may require a separate source or upstream improvement.
leads.triage: Opus follow-up Q3 confirmed only for binds declared inside a mode, low, undetectable from plain output; not published

leads.summary: The new sorting test passes when mode-group sorting is disabled
leads.consequence: Its fixture has the entry's priority and lexical chord order already favorable, so removing `entry_row` grouping produces the same assertion result. Its `grep -A2 ... | tail ... | grep -qv` guard also succeeds if it finds no entry row at all. A regression in ordering can ship with a green test. Test a mode bind with priority different from its entry or an intervening row; require exact row numbers and presence, not merely absence of a non-prefixed line.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (test validity); corroboration

leads.summary: Open PR #12362's pin-to-C test and this PR's new sort pipeline conflict on the same lines
leads.consequence: Both PRs diverged, neither is stacked (compare API says diverged). A three-way merge against #12362's own base produces conflict markers in both files. ## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** With a two-modifier or renamed-key entry chord, the mode prefix does not match the entry chord's own row, so the mode's rows do not group under it.

### Prefix does not match the entry row

`add_submap_entry` joins modifiers with ` + ` and skips the key renames rows get, so `SUPER + SHIFT + P > H` sorts above `SUPER SHIFT + P → Window mode`. The Lua route also reads every bind the scan saw, so an unbound or rebound chord can still name the mode. **Impact:** mode rows float away from their entry.

**Suggested change:** build the map from the binds `hyprctl binds` reports, deriving each chord exactly as its row.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 47ae7485)</summary>

# Reproducer: the prefix names the entry chord differently from the entry chord's own row

Reviewed head: 47ae7485054eb01e99af5fe503e04c62515d65c9 (omacom/omarchy#13461).

How to run: append the snippet to the end of `test/shell.d/keybindings-menu-test.sh` at the head commit (after the PR's own three cases, which define `mode_bind`), then run `bash test/shell.d/keybindings-menu-test.sh`. The file stops at its first failure, so append one snippet at a time. Output below is the actual stderr of that run at the head commit (stdout carried the 18 `ok` lines of the existing cases).

### Two-modifier entry chord (SUPER SHIFT + P)

Snippet:

```bash

# A mode entered by a chord with two modifiers is named the way that chord's
# own row names it, and its bindings sort under that row.
stub_hyprctl <<BINDS
$(lua_bind 64 "SUPER + F" "Full screen")
$(mode_bind 0 window "H" "Shrink width")
$(printf 'bind\n\tmodmask: 65\n\tsubmap: \n\tkey: P\n\tkeycode: 0\n\tcatchall: false\n\tdescription: Window mode\n\tdispatcher: submap\n\targ: window\n')
BINDS

rendered=$(keybindings)
grep -A1 '^SUPER SHIFT + P  *→ Window mode' <<<"$rendered" | tail -n +2 | grep -q '^SUPER SHIFT + P > H  *→ Shrink width' ||
  fail "a mode entered by a two-modifier chord sits under that chord, named as its row names it" "$rendered"
pass "a mode entered by a two-modifier chord sits under that chord, named as its row names it"
```

Actual output at 47ae7485 (stderr, exit status 1):

```text
SUPER + F                           → Full screen
SHIFT ALT + D                       → Download Video from Web App
SHIFT ALT + L                       → Copy URL from Web App
SUPER + SHIFT + P > H               → Shrink width
SUPER SHIFT + P                     → Window mode
not ok - a mode entered by a two-modifier chord sits under that chord, named as its row names it
```

### Entry chord on the key Hyprland calls grave

Snippet:

```bash

# The chord that enters a mode reads the grave key as ~ in the prefix too.
stub_hyprctl <<BINDS
$(mode_bind 0 window "H" "Shrink width")
$(printf 'bind\n\tmodmask: 64\n\tsubmap: \n\tkey: grave\n\tkeycode: 0\n\tcatchall: false\n\tdescription: Window mode\n\tdispatcher: submap\n\targ: window\n')
BINDS

rendered=$(keybindings)
grep -A1 '^SUPER + ~  *→ Window mode' <<<"$rendered" | tail -n +2 | grep -q '^SUPER + ~ > H  *→ Shrink width' ||
  fail "a mode entered on the grave key names it as ~ and sits under it" "$rendered"
pass "a mode entered on the grave key names it as ~ and sits under it"
```

Actual output at 47ae7485 (stderr, exit status 1):

```text
SHIFT ALT + D                       → Download Video from Web App
SHIFT ALT + L                       → Copy URL from Web App
SUPER + grave > H                   → Shrink width
SUPER + ~                           → Window mode
not ok - a mode entered on the grave key names it as ~ and sits under it
```

The same two-modifier result comes from the Lua road (`o.bind("SUPER + SHIFT + P", "Window mode", hl.dsp.submap("window"))` with a hyprland.lua that lets the scan reach bindings.lua): the mode row reads `SUPER + SHIFT + P > H` above `SUPER SHIFT + P → Window mode`.

Cause: `add_submap_entry` builds the prefix as `${modifiers// / + } + ${3##* + }` (bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings:282), so modmask 65 becomes `SUPER + SHIFT + P`, and it skips the key renames `dynamic_bindings` applies (lines 341-348), while the entry row renders as `SUPER SHIFT + P` / `SUPER + ~`. `prioritize_entries` then finds no row with the chord `SUPER + SHIFT + P`, so the mode rows sort on their own text.

On a copy of the head script with the prefix built as `${modifiers:+$modifiers + }$key` after the same key renames (tested together with the priority change below), both snippets pass and the PR's 18 checks still pass.

# Reproducer (follow-up Q2): a chord the Lua config later unbinds or rebinds still names the mode

Reviewed head: 47ae7485054eb01e99af5fe503e04c62515d65c9 (omacom/omarchy#13461).

The snippet defines its own `mode_bind` (the PR's helper, with a numeric `arg` as real Lua binds report). Output is the actual output of that run.

Each snippet replaces `hyprland.lua` with a minimal one (bootstrap, helpers, `require("hypr.bindings")`) so the menu's Lua scan reaches `bindings.lua`; on the shipped config the scan stops earlier (see the Lua-route finding below). The stubbed `hyprctl binds` lists what Hyprland would report after the config ran: `hl.unbind` removes every bind with that display key (`KeybindManager::removeKeybind`, src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp:204-219).

Cause: the menu's scan stub has no `unbind` (`hl` falls through `__index` to `noop`, bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings:224-228), so every described `hl.bind` the config ever made stays in `LUA_BIND_ARG_MAP`, and `build_submap_entry_map` walks that whole map (285-288) instead of the binds Hyprland reports. When two cached binds enter the same mode, bash's associative-array order picks the winner (here the stale SUPER + P).
</details>

### Mode rows with a priority description split off

Mode rows keep their own `prioritize_entries` priority. **Impact:** a mode binding described `Focus on right window` sorts above its entry row.

**Suggested change:** give mode rows their entry row's priority.

# Reproducer: a mode binding whose description matches a priority pattern leaves the entry chord's group

Reviewed head: 47ae7485054eb01e99af5fe503e04c62515d65c9 (omacom/omarchy#13461).

How to run: append the snippet to the end of `test/shell.d/keybindings-menu-test.sh` at the head commit (after the PR's own three cases, which define `mode_bind`), then run `bash test/shell.d/keybindings-menu-test.sh`. The file stops at its first failure, so append one snippet at a time. Output below is the actual stderr of that run at the head commit (stdout carried the 18 `ok` lines of the existing cases).

### Mode binding described "Focus on right window"

Snippet:

```bash

# A binding in a mode stays under the chord that enters the mode even when its
# description matches one of prioritize_entries' patterns (/Focus/ here).
stub_hyprctl <<BINDS
$(lua_bind 64 "SUPER + F" "Full screen")
$(mode_bind 0 window "H" "Shrink width")
$(mode_bind 0 window "L" "Focus on right window")
$(printf 'bind\n\tmodmask: 64\n\tsubmap: \n\tkey: P\n\tkeycode: 0\n\tcatchall: false\n\tdescription: Window mode\n\tdispatcher: submap\n\targ: window\n')
BINDS

rendered=$(keybindings)
(( $(grep -A2 '^SUPER + P  *→ Window mode' <<<"$rendered" | grep -c '^SUPER + P > ') == 2 )) ||
  fail "every binding of a mode sits right under the chord that enters it" "$rendered"
pass "every binding of a mode sits right under the chord that enters it"
```

Actual output at 47ae7485 (stderr, exit status 1):

```text
SUPER + F                           → Full screen
SUPER + P > L                       → Focus on right window
SHIFT ALT + D                       → Download Video from Web App
SHIFT ALT + L                       → Copy URL from Web App
SUPER + P                           → Window mode
SUPER + P > H                       → Shrink width
not ok - every binding of a mode sits right under the chord that enters it
```

Cause: `prioritize_entries` sorts on priority first (`sort -t $'\t' -k1,1n ...`, bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings:556) and each mode row keeps the priority of its own text, so `Focus on right window` (prio 33 via /Focus/) sorts ahead of every priority-50 row, including `SUPER + P → Window mode`. The same happens for descriptions matching /Swap window/, /Resize window/, /Move window to workspace/, /Expand window/, /Shrink window/ and the others, and in reverse when the entry row's own description matches a pattern.

On a copy of the head script that gives a mode row its entry row's priority (record `entry_prio[chord] = prio` next to `entry_row[chord]`, and print that priority for mode rows whose entry is known; tested together with the prefix change above), the snippet passes and the PR's 18 checks still pass.
</details>

### The cache-key bump is lost on rebase

quattro already moved the key to `v14` (#13521), the same change this PR makes. **Impact:** after a rebase, users who ran quattro keep the old, unprefixed rows until `hyprctl binds` output or the keymap changes.

**Suggested change:** bump to `v15`.

# Reproducer: after a rebase onto quattro the cache bump is a no-op and old rows are served

Reviewed head: 47ae7485054eb01e99af5fe503e04c62515d65c9 (omacom/omarchy#13461); quattro at b421b1b479ee9ea0863792282eee4ffeb50923dc.

quattro already moved `keybindings_cache_key` from `v13` to `v14` in #13521 (f8146395). This PR makes the same `v13` to `v14` change, so `git merge-file` of the PR's `bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings` onto quattro merges cleanly and the key line stays `printf 'v14\n'`. (The test file does conflict: both sides append a case after line 222.)

Steps: a stub `hyprctl` on PATH that reports one mode entered by SUPER + P and one binding in it:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
case "$1" in
  binds) printf 'bind\n\tmodmask: 64\n\tsubmap: \n\tkey: P\n\tkeycode: 0\n\tcatchall: false\n\tdescription: Window mode\n\tdispatcher: submap\n\targ: window\n\nbind\n\tmodmask: 0\n\tsubmap: window\n\tkey: H\n\tkeycode: 0\n\tcatchall: false\n\tdescription: Shrink width\n\tdispatcher: __lua\n\targ: 7\n\n' ;;
  devices) echo "active keymap: English (US)" ;;
esac
```

Then, each run under `env -i` with `PATH` set to the stub's directory, the checkout's `bin` and `/usr/bin:/bin`, `OMARCHY_PATH` set to the checkout, `HOME` holding a copy of `config/hypr` in `.config/hypr`, and one shared `XDG_CACHE_HOME`:

1. `bash bin/omarchy-menu-keybindings --print` from a quattro b421b1b4 checkout (writes the cache).
2. The same command from that checkout with the PR's script merged in (reads the cache).
3. The merged script again with an empty `XDG_CACHE_HOME`.

Actual output of step 1 (quattro):

```text
H                                   → Shrink width
SHIFT ALT + D                       → Download Video from Web App
SHIFT ALT + L                       → Copy URL from Web App
SUPER + P                           → Window mode
```

Actual output of step 2 (merged script, warm cache):

```text
H                                   → Shrink width
SHIFT ALT + D                       → Download Video from Web App
SHIFT ALT + L                       → Copy URL from Web App
SUPER + P                           → Window mode
```

Actual output of step 3 (merged script, empty cache):

```text
SHIFT ALT + D                       → Download Video from Web App
SHIFT ALT + L                       → Copy URL from Web App
SUPER + P                           → Window mode
SUPER + P > H                       → Shrink width
```

Step 1 writes, and step 2 finds and serves, the same records file (`keybindings-daa333993dca50a090384b4d84aff05afe5dae822ed6dfbffba963fc07ce3da0.records`), so a user who ran quattro keeps seeing the unprefixed rows until `hyprctl binds` output or the active keymap changes. Bumping to the next free version when rebasing (v15; #8229 and #7564 also propose v15) avoids it.

### The Lua route does not reach `bindings.lua` on the shipped config

The menu's Lua scan stops in `default/hypr/qconsole.lua:123` (already so at the merge-base and at quattro), before `require("hypr.bindings")`, so an entry bind there is never recorded and the mode is named instead (`window > H`). The new test stubs only a hyprland.conf-style `dispatcher: submap` entry. **Impact:** the Lua route described in the PR does not apply to user bindings in `bindings.lua`.

**Suggested change:** note the dependency on #13276 or #7564 (each lets the scan reach `bindings.lua`), and add a Lua-route test.
